name: Sam Altman
background: Ran the startup accelerator Y Combinator before leading OpenAI, which launched ChatGPT in November 2022. OpenAI's board briefly fired him in November 2023 before reinstating him days later.
why: OpenAI's plans set the pace for AI spending, data center building and AI jobs.

name: Elon Musk
background: Leads Tesla, SpaceX and xAI. Tesla announced its Optimus humanoid robot in 2021 and has said robots could become its biggest business.
why: His timelines move investor money into humanoid robots, though his past product timelines have often slipped.

name: Christine Lagarde
background: A former French finance minister who ran the IMF from 2011 to 2019, she has led the ECB since 2019, including through the 2022 inflation spike.
why: ECB rate moves change borrowing costs across the eurozone and ripple into global markets.

name: Kevin Warsh
background: A Fed governor from 2006 to 2011 during the financial crisis, he later became a critic of the Fed's crisis-era bond buying before being picked to lead it.
why: Fed rate decisions move mortgages, car loans, stocks, gold and startup funding worldwide.

name: Andy Jassy
background: Built Amazon Web Services from its 2006 launch into the world's biggest cloud business, then succeeded Jeff Bezos as Amazon CEO in 2021.
why: AWS spending decides how many data centers get built and how much AI computing power exists.

name: Sundar Pichai
background: Rose through Google's Chrome and Android teams, became Google CEO in 2015 and Alphabet CEO in 2019.
why: Google's AI spending and products shape search, advertising and the AI race.
